result: With a real setuid newuidmap/newgidmap now installed (apt, per the cited admin-install log), rootless Podman fully ran this application's actual workload for the first time, closing the specific 'no container lane has been run against this workload' claim in open_gaps[3]. Both digest-pinned images (postgres:18.6-alpine, python:3.13-slim) pulled and the app image built in 5.38s. Both containers reached a ready/healthy state in ~2.6-2.8s each. `alembic upgrade head` plus the app's 12 pytest API/DB tests passed 12/12 in the container (unlike wave 2's native 11/12, which failed for a seed-data-collision reason specific to that check's reused database, not a platform difference -- this wave's fresh ledger_test had no such collision in either lane). Resource use was captured via `podman stats`/`podman top` for the container lane and `ps` for a freshly-measured native lane (wave 2 did not record CPU/memory numbers): total process RSS was close between lanes (postgres: container 94492KB vs native 91356KB, container ~3.4% higher; app: container 86336KB vs native 86436... see native 92576KB, container ~6.7% lower), i.e. neither lane shows a decisive resource advantage at this workload's scale. Native PostgreSQL 18.6's 95.0s source-build time (wave 2, reused unmodified here) has no direct container-lane analogue, since the container lane pulls an already-published binary image rather than compiling from source; the app image's own build step (installing this application's Python dependencies into the image) took 5.38s, which is the closer like-for-like 'build' comparison. This settles open_gaps[3] for this application's workload.

verdict_impact.explanation: Establishes, for the first time on this host, a fully executed container lane (build, start, migrate, test, resource capture) for this application's actual PostgreSQL+FastAPI workload, closing the specific claim in open_gaps[3]. The measured numbers (comparable build/start times, comparable resource use, 12/12 pass) do not show a decisive advantage for either lane; combined with the paired container-recovery-isolation-cpu-mem-vs-native receipt's findings (native ~1.9x faster kill-recovery in this run; rootless user-namespace isolation confirmed for the container), this supports the existing native-first hosting-services retain decision rather than motivating a switch to a container-first default, while establishing that a rootless-Podman container lane is now a genuinely viable, measured alternative for this workload on this host.

limitations: The postgres:18.6-alpine image's first bind-mount attempt at /var/lib/postgresql/data failed fast with the image's own documented Postgres-18+ mount-path note; this is a build-recipe/documentation-following issue on this task's part, corrected within the same session, not a podman or rootless limitation.

The 'repeat-pull timing' command (0.68s) reused already-cached local blob layers from the initial (untimed) pull earlier in this session; it is NOT a cold-registry-pull measurement. The True cold pull of both images happened earlier and was not separately stopwatched, only observed qualitatively (low single-digit seconds, same order of magnitude as the app image build).

Native PostgreSQL's 95.0s build time is wave 2's own reused number (same unmodified binary, not rebuilt in this wave) and has no direct container-lane counterpart, since pulling a published image and compiling from source are different operations; comparing them as 'native build vs container build' would be misleading, so the app image's own 5.38s dependency-install build step is used as the closer comparison instead.

Resource numbers are single-sample snapshots (one podman stats/ps capture per state), not sustained load averages or repeated-trial statistics; they establish rough parity at this workload's small scale, not a rigorous performance benchmark.

The container pytest run's 12/12 vs wave 2's native 11/12 reflects different pre-existing database state between the two checks (this wave's fresh ledger_test vs wave 2's reused, previously-seeded ledger_test), not a platform-caused behavior difference; this wave's own native rerun (see the paired receipt) also passed 12/12 against a fresh database, confirming the difference is seed-data-related.

Only the DB/API pytest subset of this application's acceptance was exercised in containers (matching wave 2's own scoping); the Next.js/React build and the one Playwright browser workflow were not run in either lane in this wave.

The raw_artifacts summary transcript is a contemporaneous author-written summary compiled from the actual command outputs captured during this session, not a single captured verbatim terminal log; individual command exit codes and key numeric results (timings, RSS, checksums, pass counts) are drawn directly from this session's own tool output, not reconstructed after the fact.

The 'preregistered' text above was written before the command sequence ran (per this wave's host-safety rule), but the exact numeric thresholds for 'success' were necessarily qualitative (a working pull/build/start/test cycle), not pre-fixed pass/fail numeric bounds on build time, start time or resource use.
